info.name: Pet Shop API
info.description: version=v1 - Behaviour conformance for the Pet Shop API. Secondary artifact: it adds no examples of its own, only one test script per operation, run by Microcks against the examples declared in openapi-examples.json. Operations are matched by method and path, so the URLs below must stay in step with the contract.

exec: // One script serves every example of the operation, so it has to work out which
// one it is running against. Microcks injects query parameters as globals, but a
// global set by one example survives into the next: all_pets sends no status and
// would still read the value sold_pets left behind. The URL actually called is
// the one reading of "was this call filtered?" that cannot be contaminated.
tests["GET /api/pets: the replayed URL is readable"] = (url.length > 0);
tests["GET /api/pets: the body is a JSON array"] = Array.isArray(pets);
tests["GET /api/pets: every listed pet is complete and well formed"] = wellFormed;
tests["GET /api/pets: no pet is listed twice"] = (Object.keys(byId).length === pets.length);
// all_pets. Other examples add a pet and sell one, and the order in which
// Microcks replays operations is not specified, so only the pets that no
// example touches can be asserted on: 1..4.
tests["GET /api/pets (all_pets): the whole inventory is listed, pets 1 to 4 included"] =
tests["GET /api/pets (all_pets): pet 1 is Rex, an AVAILABLE dog at 450"] =
// available_pets and sold_pets. Soundness: nothing off-filter comes back.
tests["GET /api/pets?status=" + filter + ": every pet returned has that status"] = onlyMatching;
// Completeness: an empty answer satisfies the clause above, so name the
// pets the filter is required to have kept, and the ones it must have dropped.
tests["GET /api/pets?status=AVAILABLE: keeps the available pets 1 and 2"] =
tests["GET /api/pets?status=AVAILABLE: drops the PENDING pet 3 and the SOLD pet 4"] =
tests["GET /api/pets?status=SOLD: keeps the sold pet 4"] = (byId[4] !== undefined);
tests["GET /api/pets?status=SOLD: drops the unsold pets 1, 2 and 3"] =
tests["GET /api/pets: the only status examples are AVAILABLE and SOLD, got " + filter] = false;
// new_pet_bella: what was submitted must come back stored, unaltered.
tests["POST /api/pets (new_pet_bella): stores the submitted price, to the cent"] = (body.price === 399.99);
// The header and the body must agree on which pet was created.
tests["POST /api/pets (new_pet_bella): Location points at the pet in the body"] =
// invalid_pet: a blank name and a negative price must be refused outright.
tests["POST /api/pets (invalid_pet): the error body reports status 400"] = (body.status === 400);
tests["POST /api/pets (invalid_pet): the error body names the rejected path"] =
tests["POST /api/pets (invalid_pet): nothing was created, so no id comes back"] =
tests["POST /api/pets: answers 201 for a valid pet and 400 for an invalid one, got "
tests["GET /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the problem is titled 'Pet not found'"] =
tests["GET /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the detail names the id that was missing"] =
tests["GET /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the instance is the path that was asked for"] =
tests["GET /api/pets/1 (rex): answers with the pet that was asked for"] = (body.id === 1);
tests["GET /api/pets/1 (rex): Rex is an AVAILABLE dog priced at 450"] =
tests["GET /api/pets/{id}: the contract declares ids 1 and 999 only, got " + id] = false;
tests["PUT /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): a valid body aimed at a missing pet is a 404"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the problem is titled 'Pet not found'"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the instance is the path that was asked for"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): nothing was created along the way"] =
// sell_bella. This is the assertion schema conformance cannot make: the
// response is a valid pet either way, but only one of them is the right pet.
tests["PUT /api/pets/5 (sell_bella): the pet keeps the identity it was addressed by"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/5 (sell_bella): the sale took effect, the pet is now SOLD"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/5 (sell_bella): the pet is sold at the submitted price of 420"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/5 (sell_bella): name and category are the ones submitted"] =
tests["PUT /api/pets/{id}: the contract declares ids 5 and 999 only, got " + id] = false;
// Deleting what is not there must be reported, not absorbed into a silent 204.
tests["DELETE /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): answers 404 rather than a silent success"] =
tests["DELETE /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the problem is titled 'Pet not found'"] =
tests["DELETE /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the detail names the id that was missing"] =
tests["DELETE /api/pets/999 (unknown_pet): the instance is the path that was asked for"] =
tests["DELETE /api/pets/{id}: the contract declares id 999 only, got " + id] = false;
